body:
## Summary

`gdoc edit` replaces a matched text range by deleting it and inserting the parsed Markdown replacement. Until now every replacement went through the block-Markdown path, which emits `updateParagraphStyle` resets (`NORMAL_TEXT`) and list requests. For a replacement inside an existing paragraph that meant:

- the surrounding paragraph's heading or list formatting could be reset or turned into an accidental list;
- direct run styles on the matched text (bold, links, colors, font) were dropped because the insert only carried the styles present in the replacement Markdown.

This PR makes inline edits context-aware:

- **Paragraph lookup.** `_replacement_paragraph` finds the paragraph containing each match, including paragraphs nested in table cells.
- **Inline parsing when inside a paragraph.** `_contextual_replacement` parses the replacement with `parse_inline` and skips paragraph-level requests. Block Markdown (headings, lists, tables, multi-line text) is still used when the match covers a whole paragraph and the replacement is explicitly a block.
- **Style baseline restoration.** `_inline_baseline` compares the matched run's direct text style against the insertion neighbour and adds one `updateTextStyle` request that restores only the differing fields. Missing fields are reset through the mask rather than materialized as defaults. Mixed-style matches keep the previous behaviour.
- **Per-match cleanup shifts.** Post-batch cleanup now tracks a per-match shift instead of assuming every replacement has the same rendered length, so `--all` with a mix of partial and whole-paragraph matches lands cleanup at the right indices. Cleanup is skipped entirely when every match took the inline path.
- **CLI wiring.** `cmd_edit` passes the already-fetched search body to `replace_formatted` so no extra document fetch is needed.

Tests cover the new request shapes (`tests/test_docs_batch.py`) and the CLI routing (`tests/test_edit.py`). Verified live against a throwaway doc: both a partial-run edit and a whole-run edit preserved the surrounding raw styles and metadata.


## Partial-replacement rule

When the match is only part of a paragraph, the replacement is **inline Markdown only**. This is one finite rule, not a list of special cases:

- **Code spans follow CommonMark.** A backtick string of length N (a run neither preceded nor followed by a backtick) opens a code span that only a backtick string of the same length N closes. An unmatched backtick string is literal text. Content is inserted verbatim. So ` ```code``` ` is a code span, and a fence that is never closed by an equal-length run is literal.
- **Every block-level construct is literal text**: fences, list markers, headings, blockquotes and thematic breaks, because a partial replacement cannot start a block. Strikethrough is one or two tildes (GFM), so longer tilde runs are literal too.
- **Whole-paragraph matches** with explicit block Markdown still take the block path.

The rule is stated in `gdoc edit --help` and pinned by a parametrised test over single, double and triple backticks, tildes, unclosed strings and mixed lengths that asserts exact inserted text and exact style ranges (`tests/test_mdparse.py::test_inline_code_spans_and_literal_blocks`).
title: fix: preserve paragraph and run formatting in inline edits
